subject: general
question: Which of the following is the novel written by Hansda Sowvendra Shekhar?

options.text: All The Lives We Never Lived

solution:
The correct answer is __**My Father's Garden**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **My Father's Garden** is a novel by Indian author Hansda Sowvendra Shekhar.
 
• The book was published in **2018** by Speaking Tiger Books.
 
• The novel is divided into three parts: *Life*, *Love*, and *Loss*, exploring the themes of identity, love, and societal issues.
 
• Hansda Sowvendra Shekhar is known for his works that provide a deep insight into the lives and struggles of the Santhal community in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hansda Sowvendra Shekhar**

 
 
• He is a prolific writer and a member of the Santhal tribe, one of the largest indigenous communities in India.
 
• His debut novel, *The Mysterious Ailment of Rupi Baskey*, won the Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar in 2015.
 
• He is also a medical doctor by profession, serving as a civil servant in Jharkhand, India.
 
 
 
• **Santhal Community**
 
 
• The Santhal tribe is predominantly found in the Indian states of Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha, Bihar, and Assam.
 
• They have a rich cultural heritage with unique festivals, music, and dance forms.
 
• Their primary occupations include agriculture, hunting, and craftsmanship.
 
 
 
• **Speaking Tiger Books**
 
 
• It is an independent publishing company based in New Delhi, India.
 
• They publish a wide range of genres including fiction, non-fiction, memoirs, and children's literature.
 
• Speaking Tiger has a reputation for publishing works by prominent and emerging writers from India and around the world.
 
 
 
• **Literary Themes in Indian Fiction**
 
 
• Common themes include colonial history, post-colonial identity, social justice, and the exploration of rural and urban life.
 
• Indian fiction often portrays the complexities of caste, class, and gender.
 
• There is a growing body of work focusing on marginalized communities and indigenous cultures.
